subject: Access controls: RBAC, break-glass & support access - follow-up from demo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jones <sam.jones@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Access controls: RBAC, break-glass & support access - follow-up from demo

Hi Sam - thanks for taking the demo today, appreciate the time. Quick recap from our side and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap (high-level):
- FinTrust is evaluating Redwood to replace legacy endpoints for internal document summarization and secure Q&A.
- Main compliance asks: PII classification, 90-day retention for inference logs, customer-managed KMS, row-level RBAC and strong least-privilege controls, and auditable support "break-glass" procedures.

Open items / asks from FinTrust we heard today:
1) Can Redwood enforce RBAC at the dataset/namespace and model-call level (i.e., team A cannot call model endpoints that access team B data)?
2) Support access: what are the controls and audit trail when Redwood engineers assist with a customer incident? How does break-glass work?
3) Data residency: can we guarantee that inference logs and cached content stay within the us-east region and be stored under the customer-managed KMS?
4) Retention & logging: default retention for logs and whether log redaction/PII masking is supported at write-time.

Next steps I suggest:
- I pulled together a short RBAC overview and our SOC2 snapshot (attached). Please share any additional required docs or a template questionnaire if you have one.
- Let's do a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your security/infra lead next week (Dev and Rishi will join from our side). I can send a calendar invite - what times look good?

Attaching: redwood-rbac-overview.pdf, SOC2-snapshot-2026.pdf

Thanks again - happy to map each ask to how Redwood would implement it (config + guardrails).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Marissa - thanks for the recap and for the attachments. A few clarifications from our side to help structure the deep-dive: 

Answers / clarification on our asks:
- RBAC: we require role-based policies that can be applied to datasets and endpoints. Specifically, we need row-level scoping (e.g., by customer_id) and the ability to segregate models per business unit.
- Support access / break-glass: our security team requires a time-limited, auditable break-glass mechanism for vendor support. Break-glass must record who invoked it, reason, and require approval from FinTrust SRE or Security before elevated access is granted. Post-mortem audit logs should be retained for 2 years.
- KMS / data residency: we need customer-managed KMS; logs (inference traces, KV cache metadata) must remain in us-east-1. Any cross-region replication must be opt-in and documented.
- Retention / PII: default inference logs retention should be configurable, minimum configurable value 30 days, default 90 days for us. We also need redaction options (strip PII from logs) or token-level masking prior to storage.

Attachments: I attached our internal data-residency spreadsheet (fintrust-data-residency-requirements.xlsx) and a short security questionnaire.

For the deep-dive: Monday or Tuesday afternoon PST works for our security lead (Lisa). Can you propose 1-2 slots?

Sam
Director of Security Operations | FinTrust
sam.jones@fintrust.com | +1 617-555-2241

Subject: Re: Access controls: RBAC, break-glass & support access - follow-up from demo

Hey Sam / Lisa - great, thanks for the doc and the timing. Proposed plan for the deep-dive + how Redwood maps to each ask (short):

1) RBAC / least-privilege
- Redwood supports attribute-based policies scoped to organizations, projects, and datasets. You can scope access by customer_id using policy rules; we also support per-endpoint model access controls (allow/deny lists).
- Row-level scoping: we recommend enforcing row/namespace keys at the client-side SDK level + server-side enforcement via request attributes - we can run a short demo of this pattern in the technical call.

2) Support access & break-glass
- We have a time-bound support session flow: vendor support requests must be raised via the Console, require a pre-approved approver (customer SRE/Sec) to grant temporary elevated access, and every action is recorded in an immutable audit log.
- Post-session exportable audit trail (who, when, reason, commands run) meets the 2-year retention requirement - can be exported to your SIEM.

3) KMS & data residency
- Customer-managed KMS is supported for all persisted artifacts (logs, cache dumps). We can configure keys to live in your AWS account in us-east-1 and ensure storage and backups remain region-bound unless you opt-in to replication.

4) Retention & PII masking
- Retention windows are configurable per-tenant. Default templates can be set to 90 days; we can also enable automated PII redaction hooks (regex or built-in PII classifier) before logs are persisted.

Attachments and call: I attached a short architecture slide (redwood-rbac-overview.pdf) and our SOC2 snapshot. For the deep-dive, proposing Tuesday Dec 8 at 2:00 PM PST or Tuesday Dec 8 at 4:00 PM PST - Dev & Rishi will join to walk controls and a live demo.

Please confirm which slot works and whether we should include your Identity team.

Thanks - looking forward to the technical session.

Best,
Marissa Cole
